quote: I don't know if I want it or not. I just wanna find out what it cost.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep an explicit motivation statement (price curiosity, no conviction) and the rep files it without probing or building a bill-pain hook.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged it not worth pushing on a call this short and let the bill number do the work later — but the bill number itself was also never flipped.
coaching_implication: Should have asked what prompted the interest or acknowledged the ambivalence and tied it to bill savings before moving to logistics.

quote: The the bills average around that about 300 a month.
stewart_read: A usable bill anchor ($300/mo) was captured but never acknowledged emotionally or referenced again in the call.
coaching_implication: Rep should have said something like 'that's a real number — let's see what solar could offset' to plant urgency before the appointment ask.

quote: Do if you don't know your login, I could we could add them to the phone line here, and we could have them read it off to you.
stewart_read: Strong procedural improvisation — rep solved a real technical blocker (no login, no paper bill) with a live three-way call rather than stalling or giving up on usage data.
coaching_implication: This is a repeatable positive pattern worth highlighting to the floor, though the time cost (7+ minutes) should be weighed against organic-lead flexibility if this was not a paid lead.

quote: is this a good day to show you that design and kinda go over the price with you?
stewart_read: The booking pitch never ties back to the customer's bill or the usage data just retrieved — it's a bare logistics ask.
alternative_hypothesis: The long utility call may have exhausted rapport time, making a brief close reasonable — but the bill-flip could have been one sentence.
coaching_implication: Insert a one-line flip: 'with usage that high in the summer, this design should show you real savings' before the day/time ask.

quote: We'll plan to just have our specialist drop by tomorrow at noon,
stewart_read: Button-up covers time and day but skips the one-hour block statement, no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair' handshake — button_up is marked partial in verified events.
coaching_implication: Add the missing button-up elements (duration anchor, sit-down expectation, verbal handshake) to reduce no-show risk.

quote: We'll plan to just have our specialist drop by tomorrow at noon,
stewart_read: Rep says a specialist will 'drop by' — language suggests in-person, but the appointment was set entirely by phone with no channel clarified with the customer.
alternative_hypothesis: This could just be casual phrasing for a phone call; transcript doesn't clarify.
coaching_implication: Confirm explicitly whether the specialist meeting is phone or in-person so the customer isn't surprised.
